I am an old man now, sixty-seven years, and I have farmed this land many years. For my sorghum plot, I will put a little urea when the rains come steady, because without small fertilizer the heads will not fill well, but I cannot afford too much — prices are high and my sons help me buy. I keep my own seed from last harvest, the local sorghum that knows our soil and the dry spell, and I put cowpea between the rows as we always do. My wife and children work with me, but my back is not what it was, so I will hire a few young men for the weeding and the harvest.
